features.description: Per-vendor signal extraction in scripts/quota_check.py. New helpers: _claude_usage_v2(window) walks ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl with cache reads weighted at 0.1x and groups by message.model scoped to the window; _codex_usage_v2(window) queries ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite via SELECT model, SUM(tokens_used) FROM threads WHERE updated_at > ? GROUP BY model; _gemini_usage_v2() walks ~/.gemini/tmp/<projectHash>/chats/session-*.json files per day (NOT ~/.config/gemini/state.json which does not exist); _grok_usage_v2() returns signal:absent unless ~/.grok/ exists or XAI_API_KEY env is set. Drop the existing _codex_calls_this_week() line-counter entirely. F001 verifies tokens.total presence in a freshly-created Gemini session file before relying on it; if absent, gemini helper returns message count only with diagnostics.tokens_total=null.

features.description: Operator-editable caps file at ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json. Schema: {schema_version: 1, <vendor>: {<tier>: {<window>: {cap: number, unit: string}}}}. NOT in repo (gitignored via ~/.jarvis/ being outside the tree). NOT reusing dashboard/state/costs.json (that's $-spend on GCP, separate concern). New CLI subcommands on `python -m jarvis_orchestrate`: `quota-caps init` writes a starter file with researched defaults (claude.max_20x: rolling_7d cap=100 unit=percent_of_plan, rolling_5h cap=100 unit=percent_of_plan; codex.plus: rolling_5h cap=80 unit=messages_estimate; gemini.code_assist_individuals: rolling_24h cap=1000 unit=requests; grok.absent: {}); `quota-caps show` prints effective resolved caps; loader validates the file against expected vendor/tier/window keys at startup, rejects unknowns with a clear error.

features.description: Claude calibration command. `python -m jarvis_orchestrate calibrate-claude --dashboard-pct N [--window rolling_7d]`. Reads current observed_native for the named window from quota_state.json, computes ratio = dashboard_pct / observed_native, writes a calibration block back into quota_state.json under vendors.claude.windows[<window>].calibration: {ratio, confidence: 'manual', source: 'operator_dashboard_sample', stamped_at: <iso utc>}. Confidence levels: uncalibrated (default 0.0 ratio = no calibration applied), manual (operator-sampled), auto (reserved — NOT implemented because no Anthropic API exists). Tracker output always surfaces confidence label + stamped_at; warns to stderr if stamped_at is >7 days old. Re-calibration cadence is operator's responsibility — plan does not auto-trigger.

(3) After artificially aging the timestamp >7 days, the next run prints a stderr warning recommending re-cal. (4) Without calibration, output shows 'confidence: uncalibrated' and applies ratio=1.0.

features.description: Breaker rewrite in scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/circuit_breakers.py. check_budget_ceiling(plan, agent): for each window in state.vendors[agent].windows, compute (observed_native * (calibration.ratio or 1.0)) / cap_from_quota_caps_json; trip if any window > 1.0. INBOX wording surfaces (a) which window tripped, (b) tier, (c) observed vs cap, (d) calibration confidence label. Backward-compat fallback: if state.vendors block missing (legacy state shape), use old percent_weekly path with deprecation log. Plan-level quota_caps field still consulted as a per-plan override IF present, else fall back to operator caps file (operator caps file is the source of truth for defaults; per-plan override remains supported for plans that already declare it, but no new plan needs to declare it). Plan 004's open D001 ('which of three semantics') is answered structurally: per-vendor per-window absolute usage ceiling, semantic (1) generalized.
